hook: The Quinn House of 1875, one of the district's oldest dwellings.

historical_record.description: The Quinn House was built. It stands among the Victorian-era dwellings that survive here in numbers because the 1906 earthquake and fire did comparatively little damage in South San Francisco, and was one of the handful of buildings in the district recorded in Here Today, the 1968 San Francisco Junior League survey that was the city's first.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 63, Quinn House.

The Quinn House was under condemnation, and its ownership was unclear. The City Planning Commission unanimously approved designating the Quinn House as a City Landmark, on the Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board's recommendation.

notable_residents.name: Mary Quinn
notable_residents.detail: Mary Quinn was living in the house by 1875; the Quinn family, who owned other property nearby, kept it for eighty-three years, until 1958.
